traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 288 Lythraceae: herbs, rarely shrubby; leaves opposite or whorled, rarely alternate; stipules none or very small; flowers usually regular (Cuphea irregular); sepals joined in a tube with the petals at its top (read as a hypanthium); petals crumpled in bud; ovary superior, of 2 to 6 cells; fruit usually a capsule. APG adds the woody crape myrtle, pomegranate (inferior ovary, a berry-like fruit) and Sonneratia: so woody as often (Library 1.0's family is about a third trees and shrubs), and the inferior ovary and berry as rare (inferred).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Lythraceae with Punicaceae, Sonneratiaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345, family Lythraceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345, family Lythraceae: leaf margin entire, usually; read as {"entire": "usually"}.

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345, family Lythraceae: stipules false (absent, vestigial or soon falling), usually; read as {"false": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345, family Lythraceae: inflorescence raceme, panicle, fascicle, dichasium or solitary flowers, usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "panicle": "often", "raceme": "often", "solitary": "often"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add drupe (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345: capsule, berry or drupe-like.

traits.ovary_position.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add half_inferior (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345: superior, half-inferior or inferior.

traits.stem_cross_section.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 343, 344, 345, family Lythraceae: stems 4-angled; read as {"square": "often"}.
